verdicts.quote: “OAuth 2 authenticates against an account belonging to someone else. Any integration a third party installs needs it.”
verdicts.reason: Mailchimp’s docs explicitly designate OAuth2 for third‑party integrations; API keys are for your own account.

verdicts.quote: “You don't need a credit card to sign up for a free plan.”
verdicts.reason: Free self‑serve signup exists; once you have an account, developer docs show you can generate API keys and register an OAuth app from your account without review.

verdicts.quote: “Work with audiences, campaigns, automations, and reports… Generated from the same specification as the Marketing API reference, so every endpoint is covered.”
verdicts.reason: The official SDKs cover audiences, campaigns, automations, reports, etc., reflecting a wide, full‑product API surface.

verdicts.quote: “This documentation site is itself an MCP server.”
verdicts.reason: Mailchimp publishes an official MCP server for its developer site (and separately documents a Transactional MCP at mandrillapp.com/mcp), so MCP support is vendor‑official.

verdicts.quote: “you’re ready to dive into the Mailchimp Marketing API.”
verdicts.reason: Credentials and endpoints are documented with step‑by‑step guides; no partner gate or mandatory app review is required for standard OAuth apps, so Composio could ship today.
